questions.stem: The doctrine of separation of powers is most closely associated with

options.text: Baron de Montesquieu
Karl Marx
Thomas Hobbes
Gabriel Almond

questions.explanation: Montesquieu set out the doctrine systematically in The Spirit of the Laws in 1748, arguing that liberty is lost wherever legislative, executive and judicial powers are joined in the same hands. John Locke had earlier sketched a two-fold division.

distractorRationale.b: Marx is associated with the class analysis of the state and with socialism
distractorRationale.c: Hobbes argued in Leviathan for an undivided sovereign, which is the opposite position
distractorRationale.d: Almond is associated, with Verba, with the classification of political culture

questions.stem: The power of the Nigerian courts to declare an Act of the National Assembly null and void for inconsistency with the Constitution is called

options.text: delegated legislation
judicial review
the prerogative of mercy
legislative oversight

questions.explanation: Judicial review is the judiciary's principal check on the other organs: it tests laws and official acts against the Constitution and voids those that fail. It is what makes the Constitution supreme in practice rather than only on paper.

distractorRationale.a: Delegated legislation is rule making by the executive under powers granted by statute
distractorRationale.c: The prerogative of mercy is the executive power to pardon or commute a sentence
distractorRationale.d: Legislative oversight is the legislature's scrutiny of the executive

questions.stem: Which of the following is a check exercised by the legislature on the executive in Nigeria?

options.text: Screening and confirming ministerial nominees
Interpreting the provisions of the Constitution
Granting pardon to a convicted person
Appointing the Chief Justice of Nigeria

questions.explanation: Senate confirmation means the President cannot staff the government single-handedly, so the legislature restrains executive appointment power. Approving the budget and the power of impeachment work in the same direction.

distractorRationale.b: Interpretation of the Constitution is a judicial function
distractorRationale.c: The prerogative of mercy is an executive power exercised by the President
distractorRationale.d: The President appoints the Chief Justice on the recommendation of the National Judicial Council, subject to Senate confirmation, so the appointment is not a legislative act

questions.stem: Delegated legislation is often cited as a limitation on the doctrine of separation of powers because it

options.text: allows the executive to exercise law-making powers
allows the judiciary to appoint its own members
allows the legislature to try criminal cases
allows the electorate to vote directly on legislation

questions.explanation: When the National Assembly authorises a minister or agency to make regulations, an executive body is performing what is essentially a legislative function. That overlap breaches the third limb of the doctrine, which forbids one organ from performing another's functions.

distractorRationale.b: Judicial appointments involve the executive and legislature, and are a separate issue from delegated legislation
distractorRationale.c: The legislature's quasi-judicial role appears in impeachment and contempt, not in delegated legislation
distractorRationale.d: Direct voting on legislation is a referendum, which is unrelated to delegation

questions.stem: If the President withholds assent from a bill in Nigeria, the National Assembly may still make it law by

options.text: passing it again by a simple majority in the Senate only
passing it again by a two-thirds majority of each chamber
referring the bill to the Supreme Court for approval
submitting the bill to a national referendum

questions.explanation: The veto override requires a two-thirds majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, after which the bill becomes law without presidential assent. The high threshold means the legislature must be strongly united to overcome the executive.

distractorRationale.a: A simple majority in one chamber alone is far below the constitutional requirement
distractorRationale.c: The Supreme Court adjudicates disputes; it does not approve bills
distractorRationale.d: Nigeria's Constitution provides no referendum route for ordinary legislation

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 58

questions.stem: The organ of government responsible for interpreting the law and settling disputes is the

options.text: legislature
executive
judiciary
civil service

questions.explanation: Judicial power in Nigeria is vested in the courts by section 6 of the 1999 Constitution. Interpretation matters because a statute has no practical meaning until a court applies it to a concrete dispute.

distractorRationale.a: The legislature makes the law but does not interpret it authoritatively
distractorRationale.b: The executive implements and enforces the law
distractorRationale.d: The civil service is part of the executive machinery, carrying out policy

questions.stem: Complete and absolute separation of powers is achievable in a modern state.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Delegated legislation gives the executive law-making powers, impeachment gives the legislature a judicial role, and binding precedent gives judges a law-making role. Some overlap is unavoidable, which is why checks and balances rather than absolute separation is the working principle.

distractorRationale.a: Absolute separation would leave the organs unable to restrain one another, which would defeat the purpose of the doctrine

questions.stem: A criticism of the strict application of separation of powers in a presidential system is that it

options.text: makes the executive too easy to remove from office
can produce deadlock when the executive and the legislature disagree
prevents the courts from hearing constitutional cases
abolishes the need for a written constitution

questions.explanation: Because neither organ can dissolve or dismiss the other, a genuine disagreement over a budget or an appointment can simply stall. The parliamentary system avoids this by fusing the two, at the cost of weaker separation.

distractorRationale.a: Separation makes the executive harder to remove, since only impeachment is available
distractorRationale.c: Separation is what secures the courts' jurisdiction over constitutional cases
distractorRationale.d: A written constitution is normally essential to define and police the separation
